Wagner Logistics to Add Nearly 80 Jobs with New High-Volume Logistics Operation in Liberty

# Wagner Logistics to Add Nearly 80 Jobs with New High-Volume Logistics Operation in Liberty

 Wagner Logistics 

Oct 14, 2026, 08:54 ET

NORTH KANSAS CITY, Mo., Oct. 14, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Wagner Logistics, a nationwide provider of third-party logistics, today announced it has signed a multi-year agreement with a Kansas City-area manufacturer to launch a new manufacturing support and warehouse operations program in Liberty, Mo.

The new operation includes two leased warehouse facilities in the Liberty area totaling more than 830,000 square feet. Wagner expects to add 79 new local jobs over the next two years, starting immediately. The company will also make a multi-million-dollar investment in equipment, infrastructure and automated trailer loading and unloading technology to support the operation.

"This is exactly the kind of operation where Wagner's strengths come through," said Brian Smith, President and Chief Executive Officer of Wagner Logistics. "It requires speed, flexibility, close coordination and the ability to design a solution around what the customer actually needs."

Becker said the facility can handle nearly 7 acres of inventory under one roof. G10 shares the building with food manufacturer Eagle Foods.

As Ohio emerges as a growing center for semiconductor manufacturing, companies across the supply chain need sophisticated logistics infrastructure capable of supporting the industry's specialized requirements. DSV, a global transport and logistics provider, recognized an opportunity to establish a larger presence in the heart of the emerging Silicon Heartland.

Supporting semiconductor customers requires more than conventional warehousing. DSV needed a strategically located facility with advanced security, high-efficiency storage, and integrated transportation capabilities that could serve the industry's complex supply chain while providing flexibility for future growth.

 July 16, 2026 

Maersk will invest US$100 million in a new fulfillment hub in Hopedale, Massachusetts, expanding its contract logistics network in North America and creating approximately 1,000 jobs.

The 617,000-square-foot facility is scheduled to begin operations in late August and will support a major e-commerce customer, strengthening Maersk’s fulfillment capabilities across the US Northeast.

“Our investment in Hopedale reflects continued customer demand for modern fulfillment capabilities and reinforces Maersk’s commitment to building resilient, scalable supply chains across North America,” said Dave Hune, Head of Maersk Contract Logistics North America.

The new hub is expected to process up to 330,000 units per day during peak periods and will feature advanced conveyor and sortation technology to support high-volume fulfillment and faster deliveries across the region.
